description: A designer's quiet weekend containing one message that looks exactly like an ask — 'can you take a look?' — but is addressed to a group, answered by someone else, and explicitly closed out before the window ends. Low volume makes the single distractor disproportionately tempting.

events.text: Sorry for the weekend post. The empty-state illustration for the reports page renders at 2x on Windows and looks blurry. Can somebody take a look before Monday's demo? Not fussed who.
I'm at my desk anyway, taking it. The SVG has a hardcoded width — easy fix.
Fixed and exported. Checked it on Windows and macOS, crisp on both. Closing this out, nothing needed from anyone else.
12 files edited, 4 comments resolved, 0 comments awaiting your reply. Have a good week.

ground_truth.notes: One distractor, chosen because it has the strongest possible surface features: a direct 'can somebody take a look', a deadline ('before Monday's demo'), a weekend apology that signals urgency, and a design problem squarely in the user's area. All three defusing facts are present — it is addressed to nobody in particular, it is claimed within two hours, and it is explicitly closed with 'nothing needed from anyone else' — and the Gmail digest independently confirms zero comments awaiting reply. Low-volume windows are where over-triggering is most damaging to trust, because the user can see at a glance that the one thing surfaced was not real.
